sections.h2: Where is Amherst and who lives there?
sections.html:
Amherst is a college town of about 39,263 people (2020 census) in Hampshire County, in the Connecticut River valley about 22 miles north of Springfield.

The town covers 27.7 square miles and borders Hadley, Sunderland, Leverett, Shutesbury, Pelham, Belchertown, Granby and South Hadley. Its high point, near 1,100 feet, is on the shoulder of Mount Norwottuck in the Mount Holyoke Range. The census recognizes three communities within town: Amherst Center, North Amherst and South Amherst.

sections.h2: How does the college population shape Amherst real estate?
sections.html:
Students and staff of three colleges make up a large share of the town, and that pushes housing toward rentals and small households.

Amherst is home to the University of Massachusetts Amherst, Amherst College and Hampshire College. The 2020 census counted 9,700 households but only 4,124 families, and 35.8 percent of households were one person. The median age was 21.4 years. Education, health and social services employ 50.6 percent of working residents, and the major local employers include UMass, Amherst College, the Mullins Center, Hampshire College and the Amherst-Pelham Regional School District.

For a seller, this means two kinds of buyer: owner-occupants who want a house near the schools and campuses, and investors who count on tenants. A house that is already a rental has to meet the town's rental rules, covered below.

sections.h2: What are Amherst's rental permit and inspection rules?
sections.html:
Registration of residential rental property is required in Amherst, and permits must be renewed every year by June 15.

The town's rental property page says the Inspection Services Department has launched a Residential Rental Property Inspection Program, and that inspections are now a condition of keeping a permit. With over 5,000 rental units in town, the program is expected to run for several years, with up to 500 randomly selected units scheduled each year. Owners receive a postcard when their unit is picked. The rental bylaw was adopted on April 8, 2024.

  • Every rental permit must include a recycling plan.
  • Permitting is done online through the town's portal.
  • Inspection Services can be reached at 413-259-3030 or inspections@amherstma.gov.

If you own an Amherst rental and plan to sell, ask Inspection Services about the permit status and any open inspection before you agree to a closing date.

sections.h2: Who runs Amherst government and how does that affect owners?
sections.html:
Amherst has a town council and a town manager, and it is treated as a city under Massachusetts law while keeping "Town of" in its name.

Voters approved a charter in March 2018 by a 58 percent majority, and a 13-member council took office on December 2, 2018. Ten councilors represent districts, two per district, and three serve at large. The manager is appointed by the council. Local rules, such as the rental bylaw covered above, are adopted through this council.

sections.h2: What is the weather like and what does it mean for a house?
sections.html:
Amherst has cold, snowy winters and warm summers, so heating, roofs and insulation get close attention at inspection.

NOAA normals shown in the Amherst climate table list about 46.6 inches of precipitation and 36.5 inches of snow in a typical year. January daily highs average 34 degrees and lows 13.8 degrees. The recorded extremes run from minus 30 in winter to 104 in summer. The town sits in USDA hardiness zone 5b. A seller with an aging furnace, an older roof or an uninsulated attic should expect the buyer to raise it.

sections.h2: How do people get around Amherst?
sections.html:
Amherst is served by local buses and intercity coaches, with rail and air a drive away.

  • The Pioneer Valley Transit Authority runs local service, operated by UMass Transportation Services.
  • Peter Pan Bus Lines connects Amherst with Springfield, Boston and other New England cities, and Megabus runs to New York City and Burlington, Vermont.
  • Amtrak's Vermonter stops in nearby Northampton, and Springfield's Union Station has more frequent trains to New York and Washington.
  • Bradley International Airport in Windsor Locks, Connecticut is about an hour by car.

Amherst belongs to the Amherst Regional School District along with Leverett, Pelham and Shutesbury.

Three elementary schools serve kindergarten through grade 6: Crocker Farm, Fort River and Wildwood. Amherst Regional Middle School covers grades 7 and 8, and Amherst Regional High School serves the older students. The town also has a five-member School Committee elected to two-year terms.

sections.h2: What draws visitors and residents to central Amherst?
sections.html:
The center of town holds a cluster of cultural sites, and the Amherst Center Cultural District was formed in 2016.

Among them are the Emily Dickinson Museum, the poet's birthplace and lifelong home, the Eric Carle Museum of Picture Book Art, the Mead Art Museum at Amherst College and the Beneski Museum of Natural History. The W. E. B. Du Bois Library at UMass is the tallest academic library in the United States. Sellers near the center can point to this cluster when describing the location.

sections.h2: What about property tax in Amherst?
sections.html:
The rules below apply across Massachusetts. They come from the Appellate Tax Board's appeals guide.

  • In towns that bill quarterly, bills are generally due August 1, November 1, February 1 and May 1.
  • An abatement application is due by the first installment date of the actual bill, generally February 1 in quarterly towns.
  • Assessors have three months to act, and an appeal to the board follows within three months of their action.

Ask the Amherst Assessors for the current rate and bill dates. If a bill goes unpaid, the lien process in the Land Court's foreclosure overview applies: a demand after 30 days, a possible tax taking 14 days later, and redemption until a court judgment.

sections.h2: What does an Amherst sale require?
sections.html:
Sellers of one and two family homes need a smoke and carbon monoxide compliance certificate, and any rental use needs its permit in order.

The state's alarm inspection guide explains that you must call the local fire department once you have a closing date, and that the department charges a fee for the inspection and certificate. Alarms with no manufacture date are treated as expired.

The certificate is a requirement of the transfer whoever the buyer is, so settle in writing which side handles the inspection and the fee.

sections.h2: How do Amherst sellers choose between a listing and a cash offer?
sections.html:
The tradeoff is time and effort against price.

A listing exposes the house to many buyers, which is helpful for a well-kept home near campus. It can also bring weeks of showings and repair requests. A direct cash purchase suits owners with a worn-out rental, an inherited house or a deadline, because there are no showings and the buyer takes the house as is. Expect the price to reflect the repairs the buyer will take on.

faqs.q: How many people live in Amherst, Massachusetts?
faqs.a: The 2020 census counted 39,263 residents, and the Census Bureau's 2025 estimate is 40,920. Many are students at the three local colleges.

faqs.q: Do I need a rental permit in Amherst?
faqs.a: Yes. Amherst requires registration of residential rental property, renewed each year by June 15, and rental units are subject to inspection.

faqs.q: How often will Amherst inspect a rental property?
faqs.a: The town expects to inspect up to 500 randomly selected units each year across more than 5,000 rentals, so some owners may wait years to be selected.

faqs.q: Is Amherst a town or a city?
faqs.a: Both in a legal sense. Massachusetts treats it as a city because of its council-manager charter, but it keeps the name Town of Amherst.

faqs.q: When are Massachusetts quarterly property tax bills due?
faqs.a: In towns that bill quarterly, bills are generally due August 1, November 1, February 1 and May 1. Ask the Amherst Assessors for the exact dates.

faqs.q: Do I need a smoke detector certificate to sell in Amherst?
faqs.a: For a one or two family home, yes. The local fire department inspects and issues a certificate of compliance, and it charges a fee.
